state: The subject is a revisable business-language design, Can, whose Given/When/Then files are produced by AI for departmental applications owned by their companies. Priorities include adoption, economical authoring, visible domain policy and a single consistent way to express shared work. We have declarations and handwritten JS targets, without an executed engine or performance evidence. Under the present for limit=500 rule, finding 501 matches rolls back every write in that transaction. Shift must still reconcile retained commitments after employee, membership or location changes; Volunteer cancellation and material-change notices expose equivalent population work. A larger fixed bound cannot provide unrestricted eventual coverage. Record lifecycle events, durable keyed timers and explicit recovery already address individual identities; those facilities alone do not discover every identity. Consider only one authoritative team D1 scope for this exercise, excluding discovery across separate Durable Objects. A child's mutation stays atomic while the entire cohort is processed across transactions. Each candidate may rely on common traversal facilities and expose failed children for later recovery; none has an implementation today. The desired review uses eligibility when a child runs rather than reproducing all past eligibility transitions. Proposed coverage means capturing an owner's immutable insertion-order high-water mark at durable enumeration admission, traversing every record in that finite cohort even if its matching status changes, inspecting fresh state per child and skipping deleted records. Newer rows are protected by current creation/admission checks and later owner notifications. Derive child identity from declaration, source occurrence and record; admit children in the same commit as moving the enumeration checkpoint. A failed record must not stop unrelated records, and later notifications cannot reverse already admitted effects. Ordinary atomic loop limits continue to reject excess. This describes obligations still needing validation. Apply identical cases to every approach: 499/500/501/1000 records, repeated source delivery, checkpoint crashes, rows arriving or disappearing, restored eligibility, and a child failure.

allocation.instructions: For the next source-and-target experiment, where should the design place enumeration and follow-up work? Weigh source duplication, understandability, population completeness and work across the whole system. Choose a direction for a witness only, not an approval of a grammar or a correctness verdict.

criteria.authored: Express the continuation through existing model/scenario constructs. An app-owned review record retains the triggering identity, population boundary and traversal position, and each indexed step admits a child before arranging its successor. A common traversal contract provides the stated guarantees. Apps can tailor and inspect progress, at the cost of writing comparable continuation records and handlers repeatedly.
criteria.periodic: Arrange repeated checks keyed to each record and add a shared bounded startup/backfill procedure to establish schedules for prior records. This retains the existing timer vocabulary and also detects changes whose notifications were missed. Its costs are reconciliation delay, repeated unchanged checks and the newly specified complete initialization procedure.
criteria.enumerated: Let an event declaration name a record population, eligibility expression and normal transactional body. A shared executor performs finite-cohort scanning, deduplicated child admission and durable restart. This reduces repeated app control state and leaves domain choices in source, while requiring additional language semantics and a reusable execution/recovery lifecycle to be engineered centrally.
